anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved f1, f2, f3 and f6 from fails to holds and kept f4 and f5, so no fact regressed. Before had no deliver course at all: it reinterpreted the numeric 2 as `review`, asked a clarifying question instead of starting deliver (f1), set the deadline once at the first watch and refused to renew it on the 12:10 push (f2), demanded a separately picked `update branch`/`merge base` for BEHIND (f3), and in D labelled remote A as the `pre_head` rather than persisting pre_head B alongside expected_remote_head A (f6). After's table makes each of these explicit: course and both caps/usage persisted before writes, deadlines 12:17/12:25/12:27 with the 12:11 base move called out as a base-only observation that renews nothing, the Loop sync queued directly from BEHIND, final offering merge then stop executed without merge or approval, and D showing distinct restore (B) and lease (A) heads with a reset to B and no second push. Two small tightening points that would keep every fact while matching the Change more precisely: in the main table say the 12:17 deadline is set by the 12:02 own push (not 'minted at the first watch'), since the Change says timeout renews only on own push; and in checkpoint C state outright that exactly one re-run was authorized and no further re-run is requested, rather than leaving the count implicit in 'no second re-run'.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the course model well: a single numeric 2 persists deliver, P1 and the CI-minted P2 are closed without an intervening menu, BEHIND syncs without a separate pick, final offers merge and executes nothing on stop, B exits on repeated red while rejecting base-only SHA movement as source change, C admits the bounded watch over the open CI P1 and resolves it on the one authorized re-run, and D persists pre_head B / expected_remote_head A, leases against A and restores B without a second push. The only miss is f2: After records the 12:02 push with deadline `null` and the 12:10 push as `null at push; 12:25 when the first watch starts`, tying renewal to watch initialization instead of the own push, so the 12:17 and 12:25 values are not produced by the pushes themselves. The timeout wording should say that every successful own push (repair or sync) immediately persists `poll_deadline = push time + timeout` whether or not a watch is running, and that base observation, CI completion and watch start never touch it; then the table would read 12:02→12:17, 12:10→12:25, 12:11 unchanged (observation), 12:12→12:27, which keeps every other fact as After already has it.
